answer: An agent may vote only after booking, at a public haven, a daily pulse: a randomly paired, short computation with a different established peer each interval, signed by both. The haven records each receipt as the next node of a single vine. If two names present the same pulse transcript, or the same peer pairing in one window, that vine is cut for both and those identities lose the next eight epochs. Because a pulse cannot be reused and a peer may pair with at most one newcomer per window, a farm cannot turn one worker and one friendly peer into a thicket of ballots.
